info.title: Canaveral consumer lease API
info.description: Implemented controller consumer subset. Independently usable execution; ordinary runners remain gated for consumer lease execution. No administrator, enrollment, model, registry or host API is implied. POST bodies are JSON objects of at most 1 MiB with a single Content-Length. Browser Origin requests are rejected. Remote use requires HTTPS; the embedded server uses HTTP behind operator TLS termination. Credentials are opaque bearer secrets, never URL parameters.

post.description: Requires the current lease key and a ready eligible member. Persist the request UUID and inspect it after an unconfirmed response. Identical replay returns the current receipt and never issues a second effect. Dispatch without a completed receipt becomes unknown when authorization ends. A queued command has a 120-second start deadline bounded by lease expiry; renewals do not restart it. At most 32 pending discrete commands per host; streaming files and PTYs have separate contracts.

post.description: Requires the current lease key, a ready Android member, a host that declares leaseTunnelProtocol 1 and an application policy with limits.tunnelsPerLease above zero. Application, operator and other lease credentials are refused with 401. Persist the request UUID: a replay returns the saved tunnel in its current state and never opens a second one; a changed body is 409. Refusal codes: tunnels_not_permitted (403), capability_unsupported, member_not_ready and tunnel_port_busy (409), lease_ended (410), tunnel_limit, tunnel_host_limit, tunnel_residue_limit and tunnel_identity_limit (429). The body names a device port and a direction only; the holder-side target or listener never reaches the controller. The mapping is installed only after both peers attach.

get.description: HTTP handshake only, as for sessions: Upgrade: websocket, Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13 and Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: canaveral-session-v1, with the current lease key in the Authorization header. No Origin, body or query. One consumer peer attaches once per tunnel; the runner attaches outbound separately. After the broker's ready message the runner sends a tunnel control once the device mapping is installed; connections are then multiplexed as numbered streams with per-stream credit (session control schema, tunnel capability). Expiry, release, a fence, key rotation and supervisor loss end the relay within about a second. Nothing is replayed after a disconnect.

get.description: Live follow of this application's own events as server-sent events. Each event is one unnamed message whose id is its sequence and whose data is an Event. Named messages: open ({cursor}, always first), cursor ({cursor}, after ten quiet seconds), truncated ({after}, retention removed history after the resume cursor) and end ({code, cursor}). open, cursor and end carry the stream position as their id, so a client that reconnects with its last id resumes without loss or repetition. The Last-Event-ID header is the resume cursor and wins over after; without either the stream starts after the newest matching event. End codes: stream_lifetime after one hour, controller_closing, unauthenticated or forbidden when the credential stops being valid, unavailable. At most 4 streams per credential; a refused request is 429 event_stream_limit. Refusals before the stream begins are ordinary JSON errors. See docs/events.md. The SDK never reconnects.

post.summary: Open a live view of a leased Android emulator's screen

201.description: New durable intent created; replay returns 200

429.description: Application, resource or connection limit exceeded

Retry-After.description: Seconds before retry admission; preserve mutation identity.

post.description: Requires the current lease key and a ready member with the displayStream capability on an Android image. Application, operator and account credentials and another lease's key are refused. Persist the request UUID; a replay returns the same view. The first view of a device admits its shared live capture, which reserves one CPU and 256 MiB against the host and the application until its cleanup is proven; later views join it. 409 device_recording_active while a recording holds the device, including while its cleanup is unproven. Starting a recording while a live capture holds the same device returns 409 device_live_view_active. A new live view returns 409 capture_cleanup_pending (retryable) while an earlier live capture of the device awaits cleanup proof before its reporting deadline; 409 capture_cleanup_unproven (not retryable) after that deadline or once the capture was abandoned. A late cleanup receipt or the lease's proven cleanup can still clear the refusal; 429 live_view_limit beyond four views per device. Fixture-covered only: no native run has measured frame rate, latency or decoder compatibility.

get.description: HTTP handshake only. Requires Upgrade: websocket, Connection: Upgrade, Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13, a valid WebSocket key and Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: canaveral-session-v1. No Origin, body, credentials in URLs or query fields. Exactly one viewer peer may attach to a view. After the broker's ready message the host sends live metadata, then MP4 segments: an init or segment control followed by exactly its announced bytes in binary messages of at most 64 KiB. The viewer may send only {"type":"renew"}, which the broker answers with a renewal control. The session control schema defines liveHost, liveConsumer and liveBroker. The stream ends with the lease, its key, its device or the view's unrenewed lifetime; nothing is replayed after disconnect.

ApplicationBearer.description: Operator-created application identity, limited to its pinned catalogue and owned lifecycle.

LeaseBearer.description: Current scoped key for exactly one lease; expiry, revocation, readiness and session generation still apply.

maxConcurrentBoxes.description: Linux workspace leases with held reservations, including ended leases awaiting positive cleanup. Defaults to activeLeases; normalized in administrator responses.

tunnelsPerLease.description: Port tunnels one lease may hold at once. Absent or zero permits none; normalized to a number in administrator and catalogue responses.

baseline.description: The saved device baseline every device of this image starts from. It carries whatever its preparer installed, signed in to or configured. Android only.

isolation.description: Present only when leases of this template run in a declared isolation class weaker than their runtime's own contract. `shared-host`: an iOS simulator lease is an ordinary process tree of the Mac host's user, with the host's network and files; it is not isolated from the host or from other simulators on it, and is for trusted code only.

ttlSeconds.description: Linux leases require at least 30 seconds (400 linux_ttl_below_minimum otherwise); acquisition also refuses a configured default or maximum below 30 seconds, without clamping. Other lease kinds retain their existing bounds.

source.description: How the device was obtained: taken over from the host's warm pool without another boot, or booted for this lease. Absent while a claimed warm device is still being handed over. A warm device passes the same readiness, network isolation and image checks as a cold one. No host detail is exposed.

isolation.description: The declared isolation class of this member, when its template has one. `shared-host`: the member is not isolated from the host that runs it.

name.description: The caller's label from acquisition. Display only; it selects and authorizes nothing.

isolation.description: The isolation class of a single-member lease, repeated from its member. Absent when the template declares none.

credential.description: Returned only by explicit lease-key rotation. Store privately; never log this response.

ttlSeconds.description: Linux leases require at least 30 seconds (400 linux_ttl_below_minimum otherwise); acquisition also refuses a configured default or maximum below 30 seconds, without clamping. Other lease kinds retain their existing bounds.

MutationResult.description: A replay returns the original mutation result and a fresh lease view; their revisions and states may differ.

direction.description: reverse: the device's port reaches one target on the lease holder's machine. forward: a listener on the holder's machine reaches one port on the device.

devicePort.description: Reverse tunnels use 1024-65535 (the device's adb daemon cannot bind a privileged port). 5555 is refused in both directions.

idleSeconds.description: A connection that carried no byte in either direction for this long is reset.

mappingRemoved.description: True once the device mapping is known to be gone: the runner never installed one, reported its removal, or the lease's cleanup proved the emulator stopped and removed. Until then an ended tunnel keeps its host slot and device port.

connections.description: Concurrent connections; a further one is closed at once.

windowBytes.description: Unacknowledged bytes per connection and direction.

Error.description: Normal errors carry correlation and retry fields; unexpected service failures retain the legacy error-only 503 response.

CreateOperation.description: Durable common guest operation with a caller-owned UUID. Native capability and argument validation also apply. App/installer management is not part of this subset.

data.description: Runtime decoding enforces 512 KiB. Use upload sessions for unbounded total file size.

source.description: Opaque source context, at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes; no behavior.

position.description: 1-based place in the controller's attempt order while a lease or linux-lease request is waiting; null otherwise. An order of attempts, not a promise of admission.

Event.description: One entry of the controller's durable event log, as its owning application sees it.

sequence.description: Monotonic and never reused; the resume cursor.

data.description: Identifiers, states and bounded reason codes. Never credentials, arguments or results.

cursor.description: Pass as after to continue: the last event of a full page, otherwise as far as the read examined.

more.description: More can be read now from cursor. A filtered page can be short or empty while this is true.

truncated.description: Retention removed history after the supplied cursor.

ttlSeconds.description: The view's lifetime from readiness; each accepted renewal restarts it.

captureId.description: The device's shared live capture: a video session of kind live that holds the reservation.
